p:cNvPr.descr: Image (a) has arrows forminga large circle. In step 1, on the middle right side, there is a curved arrow going down. Next to that is another curved arrow (opposite direction) from Pi (in red) to CoA-SH. At the end of the curved arrow going down is the enzyme-bound sucinyl phosphate molecule, which has CH2 in a blue oval, and also has His-- to the right in the oval. CH2 bonds up to CH2, which bonds up to C. C bonds up and right to O- and double bonds up and left to O. The CH2 in the blue oval also bonds down to C, which double bonds left and down to O and bonds down and right to O, which bonds right to P (red, and in a red circle). Another arrow contines around, with second arrow darting left for step 2 and points to the succinate molecule. This moleule begins with C double bonding up and left to O, and also bonds down and left to -O and right to CH2. CH2 bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to C. C double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to O-. At the end of the longer curved arrow (on the left side of the image) is another blue oval, which has His-- bonding down and right to a red P in a red circle, representing phosphohistidul enzyme. Another arrow continues up and around. To the left of that arrow is another curved arrow from GDP to GTP (where P is red) for step 3. At the end of the longer arrow is another blue oval with His-- to the right, and is identified as succinyl-CoA synthetase (in blue). A long arrow continues around and down back to step 1.
